tasks.spec:
You are changing Scene 1A story data in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. Never edit storygame/ (no runtime change is needed or allowed), bench/frozen/, tests/fixtures/continuity_initiative_pre_3c_adoption/, .env, docs/testing-runbook.md, or other scenes' data. Do not reformat unrelated text. Shared runtime has no story names; this task is DATA plus TESTS only.

PROBLEM (measured on the live game, 5 of 5 playthroughs). At scene turn 4 the pacing event `pressure_1a` makes the narrator say an officer 'comes back and lingers at the drawer', though no patrol ever arrived, and nothing ever happens to the officer. We replace that one event with a short fact-driven patrol timeline in which the first arrival is shown, the officer is a real placed character while present, the officer leaves, and the word 'back' appears only after a departure.

READ FIRST: data/stories/continuity-initiative/pacing.yaml (events, `when`, `effects`, `realizations`, `verbatim`), world.yaml (npcs, locations, `facts` with `on_assert` move effects such as `rebecca_office_reached` moving brandon, `facility_perimeter_reached`), knowledge.yaml (`facts:` catalog; every world fact needs a purpose entry there), docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (on_assert, pacing realizations, how an npc is placed and which plot.md front-matter keys, `participant_ids` and `character_placements`, make an npc appear in a scene), docs/world-model-grounding.md, tests/test_scene_relative_pacing.py, tests/test_pacing_handoff.py (test_pressure_1a_prompt_carries_one_matching_realization_for_one_turn), tests/test_canon_journey.py, tests/test_scene_roleplay_contract.py, tests/test_scene_progression_phase4.py, tests/test_markdown_story_package.py (the pressure_1a pins).

THE DATA.
A. world.yaml: add an npc `patrol_officer` named `federal patrol officer`, aliases `patrol officer` and `the officer` (NOT the bare word `officer`: a bare common word is leak-scanned in earlier narration). Add a location `patrol_staging`, named `patrol staging area`, with no parent (it is where the officer is when not in the scene). Add world facts, each with a purpose in knowledge.yaml's `facts:` catalog (match the existing wording style; plain words):
   - patrol_on_scene (purpose: A federal emergency patrol has arrived at Michelle's house.) on_assert: move patrol_officer to parent outside_house with text by the front door.
   - patrol_in_house (purpose: A patrol officer is inside Michelle's house.) on_assert: move patrol_officer to parent kitchen with text at Michelle's workstation.
   - patrol_departed (purpose: The federal emergency patrol has left Michelle's house.) on_assert: move patrol_officer to parent patrol_staging.
   - card_challenged and kristin_marked_by_patrol: plain facts, no effects (purposes: A patrol officer saw Kristin take Michelle's memory card and challenged her. / The patrol has Kristin marked as someone to watch.). Task 3b uses these; declare them here.
   Before arrival the officer must not be shown to the narrator at all. Decide how the officer is placed so that is true (an npc with no initial placement, or whatever the loader requires), and VERIFY it by capturing the 1A turn prompts (see docs/testing-runbook.md section 3 and .plans/world-model-s1/prompt_capture.py) at turn 1 and at the arrival turn: the word 'officer' must not appear in the turn-1 prompt, and after arrival the officer must be listed with its place. Report how you did it. If the loader requires the npc in a scene's participant_ids or character_placements, change plot.md Scene 1A front matter minimally for that and nothing else in plot.md.
B. pacing.yaml: REMOVE the event `pressure_1a` and ADD these four events, all scene_id 1A, all realizations `verbatim: true` single-text, in this order. The turn semantics are the same as the removed event's `at_turn: 4`; check how at_turn and `when` work in tests/test_scene_relative_pacing.py before choosing:
   1. patrol_arrives_1a, at_turn 4, effects patrol_on_scene equals true. Text exactly: A federal emergency patrol pulls up outside Michelle's house. Two officers get out. One walks to the front door. The other looks over the street.
   2. patrol_enters_1a, at_turn 5, when patrol_on_scene equals true, effects patrol_in_house equals true. Text exactly: The front door opens. An officer walks in and heads straight for Michelle's workstation.
   3. patrol_leaves_1a, at_turn 7, when patrol_on_scene equals true, effects patrol_departed equals true, patrol_on_scene equals false, patrol_in_house equals false. Text exactly: The patrol pulls away from the curb.
   4. patrol_returns_1a, at_turn 9, effects patrol_return_pressure equals true. Realizations in order: when patrol_departed equals true: The patrol is coming back to the house. Then the default (no when): A federal emergency patrol turns onto Michelle's street.
   Keep home_search_narrows_1a (turn 8) exactly as it is. A fact effect with equals false must be supported by the loader; if it is not, report that and stop rather than inventing runtime code.
   NOTE: transition t_1a_1b requires patrol_return_pressure, so the timer exit from 1A now comes about five turns later than before. That is intended and approved.

TESTS FIRST. Create tests/test_1a_patrol.py BEFORE the data, confirm it fails for the right reasons, then make the data pass it. Keep it small and complete. Use a neutral scripted provider (see tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py `_provider`/`_engine` and tests/test_pacing_handoff.py for driving turns and pacing) and assert, across the real turn sequence: (1) no text shown to the player or sent in any prompt before turn 4 mentions an officer or a patrol; (2) the arrival text appears exactly once, on the arrival turn, patrol_on_scene is true and patrol_officer's parent is outside_house; (3) the entering text appears on turn 5, patrol_in_house is true and the officer's parent is kitchen; (4) the leaving text appears at turn 7, the three facts update as listed and the officer's parent is patrol_staging; (5) no authored or realized text before the leaving turn contains the words 'back', 'return' or 'again'; (6) at turn 9 the return text is 'The patrol is coming back to the house.'; (7) if the same command run is replayed with patrol_departed never asserted (assert patrol_return_pressure directly at turn 9 with a fresh state), the default text is used; (8) save/restore: after RuntimeState.snapshot() taken when the officer is in the kitchen and restore_snapshot() into a fresh state, facts and the officer's parent are identical.
UPDATE the old tests that pin pressure_1a or the old turn-4 'comes back' wording so they pin the new events instead (tests/test_pacing_handoff.py, test_scene_relative_pacing.py, test_canon_journey.py, test_scene_roleplay_contract.py, test_scene_progression_phase4.py, test_markdown_story_package.py). This is allowed and required; do not weaken assertions beyond what the new events change, and list every one you changed with the reason. Also regenerate generated expectations ONLY if a repo test demands it (do not regenerate frontend/e2e/spine-expected-reveals.json unless a test fails without it).

FINISH: ruff format and ruff check every .py you touched; run the focused tests in the check until they pass; report: the placement decision, the prompt-capture evidence, each old test changed and why.
